questions.q: Why are customers who cancelled before the snapshot dropped from the population?
options: Predicting whether an already-departed customer will cancel is meaningless, so they are out of scope
They have no rows in the orders table
They would make the churn rate too low to model
questions.explain: The model's job is to flag customers who are still active and could be saved. Someone who has already left cannot be retained by an offer.

questions.q: In the label query, which customers get churn_60d = 1?
options: Anyone with a row in the cancellations table
Active customers whose cancel_date is after the snapshot and within 60 days of it
Customers who cancelled before the snapshot
questions.explain: The CASE requires cancel_date > snapshot AND cancel_date <= snapshot + 60 days. Earlier cancellations were already filtered out by the WHERE clause.

questions.q: The label query finds 4,000 distinct customers, 310 cancelled before the snapshot, and 568 cancelling in the window. What is the baseline churn rate?
questions.explain: The population is the 3,690 customers active at the snapshot, so the rate is 568 / 3,690, about 15.4%. Dividing by 4,000 would include customers who were never at risk.

questions.q: The audit finds 371 orders dated after the snapshot. What is the right response?
options: Keep them; more data is always better
Use them only for customers who churn
Filter every feature query to order_date <= the snapshot so the model never sees the future
questions.explain: Features must be computable at prediction time. Orders dated after the snapshot are information from the future and would leak into features like recent order counts.

questions.q: Why does the scoping step produce a ranked probability rather than a yes/no verdict for every customer?
options: The retention team can only contact a limited number of customers, so they need to work down a ranked list
SQL cannot output yes or no
questions.explain: The decision is constrained by capacity (about 10% of active customers, as an illustrative assumption). A score lets the team choose how far down the list to go.
